headline: Hackers steal a record 6.3 billion dollars in crypto

sources.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea (BBC)
Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history (BBC)
Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to $6.3B hack on Binance (NPR)

chunks.text: Binance is the world's biggest [[crypto exchange]], a website where people buy, sell and keep crypto. Crypto is [[digital money]] that exists only online. An estimated 300 million people have {{signed up}} for Binance. On October 29, 2026, the company said hackers had {{made off with}} about 6.3 billion dollars in crypto. Experts call it the largest crypto [[theft]] [[on record]]. The old record was 1.5 billion dollars, stolen from another exchange in 2025.

verbs.correct: To join a service by giving your details
verbs.wrong: To buy coins when prices are low
verbs.why: Many people sign up for a free email account. My dad signs up for every new shopping app. An estimated 300 million people have signed up for Binance accounts.

verbs.wrong: To borrow money for a short time
verbs.why: Thieves often make off with bikes that people leave unlocked. Sometimes our dog makes off with a sandwich from the table. Hackers made off with about 6.3 billion dollars in crypto from Binance.

chunks.text: Binance first said the attack likely began with one engineer's laptop. Hackers had [[taken control]] of it. Later, Binance {{found out}} that there were other [[weak points]] too. A company that tracks crypto [[money transfers]] said most of the money left in about 20 minutes. The hackers used a tool that {{wiped out}} [[signs]] of their work as they went.

verbs.correct: To learn a fact you did not know
verbs.wrong: To fix a problem in a system
verbs.why: She finds out her test results online. Kids often find out the truth from their friends. Later, Binance found out that there were other weak points in its systems.

verbs.wrong: To copy files to a safe place
verbs.why: A computer virus sometimes wipes out every file on a laptop. One bad fire wipes out a whole forest. The hackers used a tool that wiped out signs of their work as they went.

chunks.text: Binance said on October 30 that it had [[frozen]] about 3 billion dollars, roughly half. Frozen money is [[locked]], so nobody can move it. The U.S. Secret Service is working to {{track down}} the rest. The tracking company and another firm say a North Korean [[hacking group]] likely {{pulled off}} the theft. The link is not proven, and North Korea has always [[denied]] such hacks. Western [[security agencies]] have said that stolen crypto helps pay for its nuclear weapons.

verbs.correct: To find something after a long search
verbs.wrong: To report a crime to the police
verbs.why: Good reporters track down people who saw a crime. My aunt tracks down old family photos at yard sales. The Secret Service is working to track down the rest of the stolen crypto.

verbs.correct: To manage to do something hard
verbs.wrong: To pay someone else to do a job
verbs.why: Small teams sometimes pull off a big win against a strong team. Few students pull off a perfect score on this test. Two firms say a North Korean hacking group likely pulled off the theft.

chunks.text: Binance has {{set aside}} 6.34 billion dollars of its own money. It promises to {{make up for}} every customer's loss. Binance stopped [[withdrawals]] on October 29. It said on October 30 that customers could soon {{take their crypto out}} again, after safety checks. The price of Bitcoin {{went down}} about 5 percent that day. Some experts say the promise may not be [[legally binding]], so the law may not [[force]] Binance to keep it. Another big exchange {{fell apart}} in 2022, and its customers lost [[huge sums]].

verbs.correct: To save money for a special use
verbs.wrong: To win money in a court case
verbs.why: Many families set aside money for a summer vacation. I set aside ten dollars each week for birthday gifts. Binance has set aside 6.34 billion dollars of its own money.

verbs.correct: To give money to cover a loss
verbs.wrong: To keep a loss a secret
verbs.why: Insurance makes up for the loss when a car is stolen. The airline makes up for lost bags with a cash payment. Binance promises to make up for every customer's loss.

verbs.wrong: To check how much you have
verbs.why: Most people take out cash at an ATM. My grandma takes money out of the bank every Friday. On October 29, Binance stopped customers from taking their crypto out.

verbs.correct: To drop to a lower price
verbs.why: Gas prices often go down in the fall. The price of a new TV goes down after a few months. The price of Bitcoin went down about 5 percent on October 30.

verbs.correct: To fail and close as a business
verbs.wrong: To change its name and owners
verbs.why: Many small companies fall apart in their first year. A business often falls apart when its owners fight. Another big crypto exchange fell apart in 2022, and its customers lost huge sums.

mainIdea.s: Hackers stole about 6.3 billion dollars in crypto from Binance, the biggest theft of its kind. About half is now locked, and the company promises to repay users with its own cash.
mainIdea.why: Hackers made off with about 6.3 billion dollars, a record. Binance has frozen about half and set aside its own money to make up for every loss.

mainIdea.s: An engineer at Binance gave a password to criminals, and that one mistake let them take billions. Customers will lose most of their savings unless the police get the money back.
mainIdea.why: Close, but Binance found out there were other weak points, not just one laptop. It also promises to make up for every customer's loss with its own money.

mainIdea.s: A large crypto exchange agreed to pay a record fine for helping criminals move cash. Officials say the firm ignored many warnings for years and must now hire outside checkers.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a hack. Hackers made off with about 6.3 billion dollars in crypto from Binance, and about half has been frozen.

tf.s: Hackers made off with about 6.3 billion dollars in crypto from Binance.

lines.text: Did you hear that hackers {{made off with}} 6.3 billion dollars from Binance?
Billion, with a B? Is that a record?
Yes. Experts say it's the biggest crypto theft ever. The old record was 1.5 billion.
How did the hackers do it?
Binance first said it began with one engineer's laptop. Then it {{found out}} there were other weak points.
For sure. For a couple of days, people couldn't even {{take their money out}}.
So what happens to the people who lost crypto?
Binance has {{set aside}} 6.34 billion dollars of its own money. It promises to {{make up for}} every loss.
But some experts say that promise may not be legally binding.
Right. Until Binance pays, it's [[a big question mark]].
Do they know who {{pulled off}} the attack?
Two tracking companies say it was likely a North Korean hacking group. North Korea has always denied hacks like this.
About half is frozen. The Secret Service is trying to {{track down}} the rest.
If a giant like Binance can get hacked, [[it could happen to anyone]].
Agreed. I want my money [[in good hands]], not on a website.
Me too. It's [[not worth the risk]]. I'll keep my savings in a regular bank.
